title: Principles of Astronomy
description: Discover the universe: planets, stars, galaxies, and our place in the cosmos; the Big Bang; how stars shine; comets, meteors, nebulae, the Milky Way; black holes and other exotic objects.

title: Astronomy Laboratory
description: Demonstration of astronomical principles through observations with astronomical instruments and analysis of astronomical data. A nighttime field trip to Mount Laguna Observatory is required.

title: Astronomy for Science Majors
description: Directed toward students with a strong interest in science and mathematics. Quantitative introduction to modern astronomy covering gravity, electromagnetic radiation, star formation and evolution, exoplanets, compact objects and high-energy transients, galaxies, and the origin and fate of the universe.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: A Walk Through the Stellar Graveyard
description: Deaths of stars and their exotic corpses to include black holes, neutron stars, and white dwarfs. User-friendly introduction to Einstein’s relativity theories, gravitational waves, and warped space-time.

title: The Dark Mysteries of the Universe
description: Ancient theories of cosmology; their relation to the development of science; our modern understanding of the origin, size, contents, and evolution of the universe; the Big Bang, dark matter, dark energy, and the universe’s ultimate fate.
notes: Does not count toward the Astronomy B.S. degree. Can count toward the Astronomy B.A. degree or the Astronomy minor.

title: Astrobiology and the Search for Extraterrestrial Life
description: Extraterrestrial life in our solar system and other planetary systems; formation of stars and planets; UFOs and SETI; origin and evolution of life on earth; life in extreme environments; cosmology and structure of universe.

title: Solar System Astronomy
description: Structures of the planets; their surfaces, atmospheres, and satellite systems; asteroids, comets, and meteoroids. The Sun, its structure, energy production, and influence in the solar system. Life in the solar system.

title: Astronomical Techniques
description: Astronomical observation and optics. Data acquisition and reduction for modern astronomical instrumentation including photometry, direct imaging, and spectroscopy. Techniques for obtaining precise measurements and determining measurement uncertainties.

title: Astrophysics of Stars
description: Lives, interior structures, and physics that determines how stars work. Stellar atmospheres and spectrum of light that emerges from stars.

title: Extragalactic Astronomy
description: Review of basic astrophysics; flux and intensity measurements, blackbody radiation, the astronomical magnitude system, interstellar extinction, and distances determinations within the galaxy; morphological properties of galaxies; stellar populations; extragalactic distance indicators and the cosmological distance scale; introduction to cosmology.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Senior Project
description: Selection and design of individual projects.

title: Senior Project
description: Individual research project culminating in a final written report.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Exoplanets
description: Extrasolar planet detection; mass and radius determination; transits and eclipses; orbital dynamics and transit timing variations; internal and atmospheric characteristics; the exoplanet population and formation scenarios.

title: Advanced Topics in Astronomy
description: Selected topics in astronomy or astrophysics.

title: Binary Stars
description: Visual, spectroscopic, and eclipsing binary stars. Review of observational techniques. Methods of orbital analysis with applications emphasizing determination of fundamental stellar properties, such as mass, radius, temperature, and luminosity. Implications for stellar evolution.

title: Stellar Atmospheres and Interiors
description: Gas thermodynamics and equations of state. Production of stellar continuum radiation and spectral lines. Theories of radiative and convective energy transport. Interior structure and evolution of stars.

title: Galactic Structure and Evolution
description: Stellar and gaseous structures of the Milky Way and external galaxies. Properties to include chemical evolution, color distributions, luminosity functions, mass-to-light ratios, scaling relations, and surface brightness profiles. Dark matter halos, gravitational collapse models, and hierarchical structure formation. Contents and physical state of interstellar and circumgalactic media.

title: Foundations of Modern Cosmology
description: Big Bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, early universe, expansion dynamics, extragalactic distance scale, largescale structure, Newtonian and relativistic cosmology. Observational constraints on cosmological parameters and equation of state.

title: Astronomical Techniques
description: Basic methods of data acquisition and analysis. Emphasis is given to CCD direct imaging, spectroscopy, and photometry. Direct experience with telescopes and instruments at Mount Laguna Observatory, as well as with the department computing and image processing facility.

title: Research
description: Research in one of the fields of astronomy.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.
